title: Fearless AI SDK Contract Hardening
problem: Siumai preserves AI SDK-style stream, metadata, tool, usage, cancellation, and error data but leaves several replay, diagnostics, safety, and capability semantics implicit.
objective: Make the shared contracts explicit, tested, documented, and reflected in changelogs so downstream adapters can consume Siumai without undocumented replay or raw-data assumptions.
next_task: No split Siumai follow-up. Provider-specific unsupported option rewrites may be opened as new provider-scoped workstreams if concrete behavior gaps are found; Hajimi adapter changes remain out of scope.
gates: cargo nextest run -p siumai-spec -p siumai-core -p siumai-protocol-openai --no-fail-fast

evidence.summary: Recorded 12 AI SDK contract gaps across stream replay, reasoning/text separation, cancellation, raw diagnostics, tool contracts, usage, error safety, and capability failure behavior.
Documented StreamEnd response content as final replay/fallback and added a stream processor regression test proving it is not appended as another text delta.
Added an OpenAI Responses SSE fixture proving reasoning deltas and terminal-only final visible text are both preserved.
Documented stream_with_cancel as the recommended cancelable stream entry, separated local cancellation from provider-specific remote abort, and added a core local cancellation regression test.

Defined public provider metadata versus private raw diagnostics boundaries and added tests for response metadata, raw stream parts, replay raw items, custom diagnostic event types, and OpenAI-compatible raw chunks.
Split safe user-facing error messages from raw diagnostics so user_message() and normal summaries no longer expose provider raw detail, while diagnostics fields retain raw messages and bodies.
Added explicit tool-name/provider-tool-id validation and fallible constructors, documented provider-executed ownership, and tested ToolInputStart stable projection without provider replay indexes.
Defined Usage as a per-provider-call cumulative snapshot, replaced repeated finish usage snapshots in the stream processor, and added an OpenAI Responses repeated-usage fixture.

Added explicit unsupported-capability policy behaviors for reject, warn, and provider fallback; core hard family guards now reject through the shared policy while provider-specific option rewrites remain follow-ons.

Closed the lane after fresh spec/core/protocol gates passed, changelogs were reconciled, and full workspace formatting was recorded as blocked by Windows path-length error 206 with crate-scoped fmt passing.

continue_policy.notes: The Siumai contract-hardening scope is complete. Open new provider-scoped workstreams for concrete unsupported-option behavior gaps. Hajimi adapter changes remain out of scope.
